title: Practice 5: при- and у-: arriving, and leaving

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.why: **уйти** (the infinitive) (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **прийти** (**прийти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **приедешь** (**приехать**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

The other choice: **прибежал** (**прибежать**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: We brought cheese and wine from France.
exercises.why: **привозим** is the present tense (1st person plural) of **привозить** (to bring, to fetch by vehicle) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **привезти**. present: я привожу́ · ты приво́зишь · он приво́зит · мы приво́зим · вы приво́зите · они приво́зят. — Wiktionary, «привозить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «привозить — привезти — to bring (by vehicle).» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **увозим** (**увозить**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: A person named Williams came to see you yesterday.
exercises.why: **приходил** is the past tense (masculine) of **приходить** (to come (to), to arrive (at) (place, conclusion, state of abandonment, anger, insanity)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **прийти**. past: он приходи́л · она приходи́ла · оно приходи́ло · они приходи́ли. — Wiktionary, «приходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда? — Это старшина. Лейтенант в штабе? — Нет, он уже идёт (едет) сюда.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **уходил** (**уходить**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **привели** is the past tense (plural) of **привести** (to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приводить**. past: он привёл · она привела́ · оно привело́ · они привели́. — Wiktionary, «привести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «приводить — привести — to bring (along), to lead.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **увели** (**увести**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: You're coming to Montreal this weekend?
exercises.why: **приедете** is the future tense (2nd person plural) of **приехать** (to arrive, to come (by vehicle or horse); (past tense, plural only) to hit rock bottom) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приезжать**. future: я прие́ду · ты прие́дешь · он прие́дет · мы прие́дем · вы прие́дете · они прие́дут. — Wiktionary, «приехать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Сегодня он приехал сюда на автобусе.» (Perfective) — DLI, Lesson 56. «Сегодня он приедет сюда на автобусе.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  The other choice: **уедете** (**уехать**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
